one_month_reasoning: The next scheduled company catalyst, fiscal Q1 FY27 results, is expected around 2026-11-03, just after the 2026-11-01 horizon (Nov 1 is a Sunday, so the effective mark is the Oct 30 close). Inside the window: peer prints (e.g. hyperscaler Q3 capex commentary in late October, which has been supportive per Goldman/Moody's capex upgrades), the usual pre-earnings positioning, and macro prints (CPI, FOMC late Oct). The stock is at its 52-week high after +533% in a year; short-horizon base rates offer offsetting momentum (continuation) and post-spike reversal, and the July 2026 episode showed 33-43% drawdowns can happen with no fundamental news. With no decisive event in the window I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred just below spot (~$1080) at about annual vol / 3.5 (sigma ~25% for the month), giving P(>= spot) of about 0.49.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) NTM-at-horizon EPS of ~$28 x 32x (LITE's ~31x five-year average forward P/E, a cycle-peak discount to today's ~42-45x) = ~$896, weight 0.6, and (b) a base-rate anchor of spot plus roughly market-like drift (~5%) = ~$1,140, reflecting Bessembinder's finding that extreme 5x winners show ~zero subsequent market-adjusted returns, weight 0.4. Blended ~$990.

bear.story: AI optics cycle turns: hyperscaler capex growth decelerates faster than expected (Goldman already sees 2027 +54% slowing to +12% in 2028), supply loosens, pricing-driven gross margins (47-50%) mean-revert toward the low-40s, and the multiple compresses to ~20-25x on ~$22 EPS. The 2001 JDSU precedent (revenue $3.2B to $1.1B in a year, stock -98%) is the tail of this case; a recession in 2027 accelerates it.

base.story: Growth continues (revenue run-rate toward $1.6-1.8B/quarter by mid-2027, CPO/OCS ramps) but the multiple de-rates from ~45x forward to ~32-38x as growth slows; EPS gains roughly offset multiple compression, consistent with the base rate that 5x winners deliver ~market returns afterwards.

bull.story: 2027 capex lands near Goldman's $1.2-1.4T, 1.6T transceivers/EMLs stay supply-constrained, CPO and OCS add a second engine, EPS run-rate reaches $40+ and the market keeps a ~45x multiple; ~30% of 5x winners go on to another big multiple per Bessembinder.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$560 (roughly half today's price, ~25x a ~$22 FY27 EPS, and well below the July 2026 panic low of ~$720 that happened with no fundamental damage), the move would most likely reflect a real break: a guidance cut, gross-margin reversal as laser/EML supply catches up, a hyperscaler capex pause, or share loss in transceivers/CPO, rather than ordinary 97%-vol noise.

reasoning: Lane: base rates. Company facts: Q4 FY26 revenue $1.01B (+109% y/y), non-GAAP EPS $3.23, Q1 FY27 guide $1.25B and $4.20 EPS, cash $2.7B vs ~$1.6B current debt, 101M diluted shares, so ~$110B market cap at ~45x forward. Base rates: (1) Bessembinder's study of 5x winners finds ~zero subsequent market-adjusted returns but ~30% go on to repeat, i.e. a wide, roughly centred distribution rather than continued drift; (2) the optical precedent (JDSU FY01-02: revenue -66%, stock -98%) shows how violent the left tail is when telecom/datacom capex turns; (3) LITE's own forward P/E history ranges 10-54x with ~31x five-year average, and July 2026 already saw a 33-43% drawdown without bad news; (4) hyperscaler capex forecasts still rise in 2027 (+54% to ~$1.2T per Goldman) but growth slows sharply into 2028, which is exactly when the market will price LITE at the horizon. Valuation blend gives ~$990. I set a lognormal-like distribution with median ~$1,010 and sigma ~0.68 (below the trailing 97% realized vol, as vol after a parabolic year typically mean-reverts but remains extreme), with a slightly fatter left tail for the bust scenario. P(>= spot) ~0.455; P(>= half of spot) ~0.81; P(>= 2.5x spot) ~0.07. Research limited to ~12 queries; prediction-market current prices could not be fetched directly (aggregator 503), so recession odds are used qualitatively only. No option data was consulted.
